read.headline: Lay-backs 4 of 5 in the fairway; wedge shots 13 of 18 on the green (clubs read from the bag). The non-negotiables held 1 of 4 round grades.
read.decision: Don’t plan a shot that leaves 40–74 yards. Leave a distance you hit greens from, full wedge or three-quarter.

graded.name: Lay back and you hit the fairway
Carry by 15, or lay back by 15

items.label: Non-negotiable 1
items.name: Lay back and you hit the fairway
items.says: If you leave the driver in the bag to play safe, the safer club has to find the fairway. Every time.
items.plan: Every par 4 and par 5 gets one tee club. If your driver finds 70% of fairways or more, hit it: the distance is free. Lay back only when driver would leave the dead zone, or finds fewer fairways than the shorter club.
items.gate: If you leave the driver in the bag to play safe, the safer club has to find the fairway. Every time.

items.label: Non-negotiable 2
items.name: Wedges always find the green
items.says: Any shot with a wedge finishes on the green: full swing, pitch, chip or bunker shot. The green is the minimum; inside 6 feet is the target.
items.plan: Leave yourself the wedge distance you actually hit greens from. Around the green, pick the lower shot that lands on the green and runs, not the high one that has to land perfectly. A wedge means PW, GW, SW or LW; a 9-iron is not a wedge.
items.gate: Any shot with a wedge finishes on the green: full swing, pitch, chip or bunker shot. The green is the minimum; inside 6 feet is the target.

items.label: Non-negotiable 3
items.name: Never leave 40–74 yards
items.says: Don’t plan a shot that leaves 40–74 yards. Leave a distance you hit greens from, full wedge or three-quarter.
items.plan: On a short par 4, lay back to your best number. On a par 5, lay up to your band, not as close as you can get. A lay-up has a second dead zone: never leave 121 yards or more. Two players on the same hole get different numbers, and that is the rule working.
items.gate: Don’t plan a shot that leaves 40–74 yards. Leave a distance you hit greens from, full wedge or three-quarter.

items.label: House rule 2
items.name: Every par 5 on the green in three, with the go line
items.says: Every par 5 is on the green in three or fewer. Going for it in two is your call if either is true: you hit 40% of greens from that distance, or the likely miss finishes within 40 yards of the green. If both are true, the go is the plan. On a par 4 of 360 yards or less, if your tee club finishes inside 40 yards, going is the plan, unless water or out of bounds is in play.
items.plan: Lay up to the distance you hit greens from, not as close as possible. The likely miss is read from your longest club off the deck. Clear both tests and you go; clear one and it is your call; clear neither and the lay-up is the plan, with the go still shown at its real odds.
items.gate: Every par 5 on the green in three: 100%.

items.label: House rule 3
items.name: Approach inside 40 feet
items.says: Plan every approach to finish inside 40 feet. For most golfers, inside 40 feet is a great shot.
items.plan: Aim at the part of the green that leaves 40 feet or less, not at a tucked flag. When the pin is tight to trouble, the middle of the green is usually inside 40 feet and is the shot.
items.gate: Every approach planned to finish inside 40 feet.

items.label: House rule 8
items.name: Long par 4s: bogey is the enemy
items.says: On a par 4 of 400 yards or more, bogey is the enemy. Take the tee club that finds a good drive, not the longest one; play the approach to finish inside 40 feet, on the long side / open side; a par is a good score.
items.plan: One tee club that finds a good drive, an approach to the safe part of the green, two putts. Printed as a reading: bogey or worse on par 4s of 400 yards or more.
items.gate: Bogey or worse on long par 4s under the winners’ 8%.

leaveAlone.label: Non-negotiable 4
leaveAlone.name: Carry by 15, or lay back by 15
leaveAlone.says: Clear every hazard by at least 15 yards, or stop at least 15 yards short of it. Never play to the edge.
leaveAlone.plan: There are two clubs: the one that clears by 15 and the one that stops 15 short. The club in between is never the answer. If your misses spread wider than most, take a wider margin.
leaveAlone.gate: Clear every hazard by at least 15 yards, or stop at least 15 yards short of it. Never play to the edge.

leaveAlone.label: Non-negotiable 5
leaveAlone.name: Choose to play stress free
leaveAlone.says: Play the shot you know works, not the one that might. When two options are close, take the one you can commit to.
leaveAlone.plan: The plan picks the option you can commit to without hesitation, and says so, so the choice is made before you get there. Plan every six holes to be level or better: holes 1–6, 7–12 and 13–18. A calm start is the easiest stress to avoid, and it has to last all 18.
leaveAlone.gate: Play the shot you know works, not the one that might. When two options are close, take the one you can commit to.

leaveAlone.label: House rule 1
leaveAlone.name: Inside 6 feet is sacred
leaveAlone.says: Make every putt from 6 feet and in. 100%, every round. One miss is noted.
leaveAlone.plan: Putting practice starts inside 6 feet and doesn’t move on until it holds. It is repetition, not technique.
leaveAlone.gate: Every putt from 6 feet and in holed: 100%.

leaveAlone.label: House rule 4
leaveAlone.name: Beyond 24 feet, the target is the leave
leaveAlone.says: From 24 feet and out, putt to a distance, not the hole. Finish within a tenth of the putt: from 30 feet, inside 3.
leaveAlone.plan: On a long first putt, commit to the distance, not a line into the cup. That keeps the second putt inside tap-in range.
leaveAlone.gate: Every first putt from 24 feet and out left within a tenth.

leaveAlone.label: House rule 5
leaveAlone.name: Take the bogey before the double
leaveAlone.says: When a hole goes wrong, the job is a bogey at worst. From a bad lie (waste area, native grass, cart path, a bunker off the tee), take the club that gets you back to a normal lie, never a driver or fairway wood; then the middle of the green and two putts.
leaveAlone.plan: An iron, hybrid or wedge back to the fairway or a full-swing number, even if it gives up ground; then the middle of the green. The escape is judged on the lie it leaves, not the yards.
leaveAlone.gate: From a bad lie, never a driver or fairway wood; no double.

leaveAlone.label: House rule 6
leaveAlone.name: Short game finishes inside 6 feet
leaveAlone.says: Every chip and pitch aims at a 6-foot circle. The green is the minimum; inside 6 feet is the target.
leaveAlone.plan: Take the lower shot that runs to the hole rather than the high one that has to land perfectly.
leaveAlone.gate: Every chip and bunker shot on the green, half of them inside 6 feet.

leaveAlone.label: House rule 7
leaveAlone.name: Birdie conversion
leaveAlone.says: Birdies (eagles count) divided by greens hit in regulation. Elite is 35%; a winning week is 41%.
leaveAlone.plan: Low conversion with long approaches means the irons are the work; low with close approaches means the putter.
leaveAlone.gate: Birdie conversion at 41%, a winning week.

leaveAlone.label: House rule 9
leaveAlone.name: The reset hole
leaveAlone.says: After a bogey or a double, the next hole is about righting the ship: your normal club, fully committed, then the middle of the green. A par is the job.
leaveAlone.plan: No heroics on the hole after a bogey. A par there is a win; the birdie comes from the putt, not from forcing the approach.
leaveAlone.gate: After a bogey, par or better on the next hole every time.

leaveAlone.label: House rule 10
leaveAlone.name: A par-5 lay-up stays in the fairway, as close as it allows
leaveAlone.says: From the fairway on a par 5, the lay-up has to stay in the fairway, and leave the third shot as close as the fairway allows. Two dead zones: 40–74 yards and 121 yards or more.
leaveAlone.plan: Take the club that is sure to find the fairway, then the number inside your best band, as close as that band allows. Rough, sand or a penalty area fails it, whatever number it leaves.
leaveAlone.gate: Every par-5 lay-up in the fairway: 100%.

notMeasured.label: House rule 11
notMeasured.name: Miss on the long side / open side
notMeasured.says: Your safe miss is the long side or the open side of the green. Never short-side yourself. When the pin is at the front, the long side is past it: play at least 5 yards past, wedges included.
notMeasured.plan: On a tucked flag, start the approach at the long side and let the miss be long. Front pin: add 5 yards or more to the number, then pick the club; chipping, land it 5 yards further on and still finish inside 6 feet.
notMeasured.gate: Every miss on the long side / open side.
